questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Choose the form that correctly completes the sentence: “Thirty years ago, more women ___ housewives than now.” (A) did (B) would (C) used to (D) are

evidence: Thirty years ago, more women used to be housewives than now.
To describe repeated states or situations in the past, however, we use only used to.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your family has decided to adopt a puppy. Write a notice of 100 words for your school notice board, telling readers what has to be done before the puppy comes home and why the whole family must agree.

markingPoints.description: Content: lists the practical steps a family must take before the puppy arrives — annual dog licence, annual vaccination, toilet training, obedience training, grooming and bathing, a balanced diet, socialisation, and a daily dose of exercise, affection and play.
Format: opens with a clear heading (NOTICE) and gives the notice-writer’s details at the end, as a school notice must.
Organisation: the steps are set out as short numbered or bulleted points in a sensible order, so a reader can tick them off one by one.
Accuracy: correct spelling, grammar and punctuation, and no step that is not part of caring for a puppy.
Expression: concise, formal and suitable for a school notice board, and kept to about 100 words.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
NOTICE
Adopting a Puppy
Our family is thinking of adopting a puppy. A pet is a lifetime of commitment — up to ten years or more if you own a dog or a cat — so every member of the family must agree before it comes home, or the pet could end up unwanted. Our checklist:
• get an annual dog licence, as government regulations require
• arrange annual vaccination against major diseases
• set aside time for toilet training, obedience training, grooming and bathing
• feed a balanced diet
• never keep the puppy confined; socialisation is very important
• give it a daily dose of exercise, affection and play.
— Class Representative

evidence: Owning a pet is a lifetime of commitment (up to ten years or more if you own a dog or a cat) involving considerable responsibility.
The decision to acquire one, therefore, should be made by the whole family. Without full agreement by everyone, the pet could end up unwanted.
socialisation (many dogs are kept confined in cages or tied up to stop them from dirtying the garden or from chewing on shoes — this is wrong) is very important
